newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares close at sixth straight record high.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares close at sixth straight record high.

text.p: Egyptian shares closed at the sixth straight record high on Sunday and brokers expected more cash inflows would push prices higher.
The Capital Market Authority all-share index jumped 1.22 percent to close at 359.64 points from 355.31 on Thursday. Turnover was a moderate 62.63 million pounds ($18.42 million).
"More foreign funds are coming in, pushing prices upwards," said Muheb Milad of Megavest.
Cement firms dominated the trade and Amriyah Cement was the most active share. It rose 3.70 pounds to close at 81.70, when shares worth 12.42 million were traded.
"Amriyah has been in demand for three days," Khaled Taha, deputy managing director of Triple A Securities, told Reuters.
Helwan Portland Cement came second among today's most active shares, with shares worth 6.27 million changing hands.
Medinet Nasr Housing and Development resumed its upward trend after recent corrections, rising 2.00 pounds to finish at 425.00.
Among other big gainers was National Cement, which ended 2.65 pounds up at 35.02. Storage rose 3.50 pounds to 73.50.
The stock market board is still imposing a ceiling on trade in two banks -- Commercial International Bank and National Societe Generale Bank at 600 and 750 pounds respectively.
"The board sees that the prices of these banks are too high,"Taha said.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 589.64 points from 580.24 points on Thursday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms also rose to 239.76 from 237.50.
Out of the 83 shares traded, 46 gained, 13 lost and 24 ended the day unchanged.
